title: Large guaranteed-income transfers did not produce the expected political mobilization or trust shift
source_unit: NBER Working Paper 33214; randomized guaranteed-income field experiment with 1,000 low-income treatment participants and 2,000 controls, linked to political-attitude and behavior measures
geography: United States; low-income adults enrolled in a randomized guaranteed-income experiment

observations.period: Three-year guaranteed-income experiment; working paper issued November 2024

denominator.unit: 1,000 treatment participants receiving $1,000 per month and 2,000 controls receiving $50 per month

institutional_trust.value: no detectable effect on trust in government, polarization, or support for democracy

racial_affect.value: small improvements in affect toward own and other racial groups and some politicians

work_meaning.value: some evidence treated participants viewed work as more important or as a requirement for accessing government programs

observations.method: Randomized field experiment providing tax-free monthly income for three years, with political participation, engagement, preferences, trust, polarization, support for democracy, affect, and qualitative mechanism measures.
observations.uncertainty: The null results are bounded by the study population, intervention duration, political context, outcome measures, statistical precision, and treatment take-up. No detectable effect is not proof of no effect for every political behavior or subgroup. The experiment does not identify whether household-level work, relationship, healthcare, or material changes mediated political outcomes.
observations.subgroup: Low-income U.S. adults enrolled in the experiment; treatment and control groups as defined by the study, with subgroup and mechanism limits preserved.
observations.counterinterpretation: Political predispositions may be durable and less responsive to income than observational correlations suggest; small affect or work-attitude changes may coexist with unchanged participation and trust. Other transfer designs or tax treatment may produce different responses.

related_sources.claim: NBER DOI record for Working Paper 33214
Related analysis of intrahousehold guaranteed-income outcomes; not pooled with political outcomes

boundary: This record adds a causal income-to-political-attitudes/behavior test: a large three-year guaranteed-income transfer did not detectably change political participation, engagement, broad preferences, government trust, polarization, or support for democracy in the study population. It does not establish that material conditions never affect politics, that all subgroups are unaffected, or that household work, relationship, health, or meaning pathways are absent.
